subject: Micro-retainer vendor: PO-exemption and identity verification
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@microretainers.co>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Accounts Payable <ap@microretainers.co>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question — monthly micro-retainer (no PO?)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the intro earlier this week. MicroRetainers provides a $400/month advisory retainer for quick product reviews — we typically onboard customers quickly and invoice at month-end. For Redwood's onboarding, is a purchase order required for recurring micro-retainers like this, or is there an "invoice-only" option for low-dollar recurring services?

We'd prefer not to delay with a full PO (this is a short 3-month pilot), but we can provide standard legal and tax documents right away (W-9, company registration). Can you point me to the onboarding checklist and any evidence you need to qualify for a no-PO lane?

Attaching the standard vendor intake form we usually send to larger customers — happy to fill any Redwood-specific fields.

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Partnerships, MicroRetainers Co.
attachments: vendor_contractor_form.pdf (pdf), onepager.pdf (pdf)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@microretainers.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 09:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question — monthly micro-retainer (no PO?)

Samira — thanks for the clear note and the attachment.

Short answer: we can consider a temporary invoice-only path for a 3-month micro-retainer pilot, provided we get: 1) entity verification (incorporation docs), 2) completed vendor intake with banking and tax ID, and 3) a signed SOW or service confirmation outlining scope and monthly cap. Finance needs to approve a provisional exception for recurring services under $1,000/month.

Looping in Marissa from Procurement to confirm the exception criteria and Ben from Finance for accounting treatment. Marissa — can Procurement approve a 90-day invoice-only onboarding for MicroRetainers if they supply the items above and accept standard payment terms? If yes, we will document the conditional approval and require a follow-up check at day 60.

Also copying the internal onboarding checklist (we keep it internal) — I'll add MicroRetainers to HubSpot and attach the DocuSign SOW template if needed.

- Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick question — monthly micro-retainer (no PO?)

Quick take from Procurement: we can grant a provisional invoice-only onboarding for up to 90 days for this use case with the following gates: 

- Required evidence before first invoice: completed vendor intake form, W-9 (or equivalent), proof of US incorporation (state filing), and bank ACH details.
- Controls: limit monthly invoiced amount to $1,000 and cap total pilot to $3,000 across the 90-day exception.
- Operational: vendor must provide a signed SOW (DocuSign link below) that includes an itemized monthly cap and a single Redwood billing contact.
- Risk checks: Procurement will run identity verification and match legal name to tax docs. If any red flags come back, we revoke the exception immediately and require a PO.

Ben — can Finance accept invoices against a provisional exception and code them temporarily to GL 5201 (Consulting - Pilot)? We'll need to reconcile and reclass once/if a PO is generated. Also suggest we require Net30 payment terms for a pilot to minimize exceptions revenue impact.

Samira — please submit the two documents (W-9 and company registration) and sign the SOW. Once procurement confirms the verification result we will confirm the invoice-only lane. I'll record the exception in the procurement tracker and set a 60-day review.

DocuSign SOW: https://app.docusign.com/recipient/12345
Procurement tracker (internal): https://redwood.app/hubspot/records/HD-3245

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
